ctor.rationale: `base(1, CardType.Power, CardRarity.Rare, TargetType.Self)` (CrimsonMantle.cs:19-22) == cost 1 / POWER / RARE / SELF. No keywords. It does NOT override GainsBlock even though the power grants block, so the sim's `gains_block` default of False is right and Nimble's CanEnchant refuses it on both sides.

OnPlay.rationale: `PowerCmd.Apply<CrimsonMantlePower>(..., DynamicVars["CrimsonMantlePower"].BaseValue, ...)` followed by `?.IncrementSelfDamage()` on the RETURNED power (CrimsonMantle.cs:28) == `PowerCmd.apply(...)` then `ctx.player.powers.get('crimson_mantle')` and `power.increment_self_damage()` (crimson_mantle.py:37-42). The sim has no return value from `PowerCmd.apply`, so it re-fetches the power by id; on the normal path both reach the same instance and increment it exactly once per play. Presentation, folded in: NPowerUpVfx (26) and TriggerAnim (27).

guards.what: C# skips IncrementSelfDamage when Apply returns NULL; the sim increments whenever the power is present (CrimsonMantle.cs:28 vs crimson_mantle.py:40-42)
guards.issue: `PowerCmd.Apply<T>` returns null in three documented cases (PowerCmd.cs:29-34, 68-87): combat is ending, `!target.CanReceivePowers`, or the stacking `ModifyAmount` resolved to 0. The null-conditional `?.` then skips the increment. The sim's re-fetch by id (`ctx.player.powers.get('crimson_mantle')`) cannot distinguish those cases from a successful apply -- if a SECOND Crimson Mantle is played and something modifies its amount to 0, C# leaves the self-damage counter alone and the sim still bumps it, so the player takes one extra HP per turn for the rest of the combat. DORMANT: no ported effect modifies a positive self-applied BUFF's amount down to exactly 0 (Artifact only intercepts debuffs, `PowerType.DEBUFF`, cmds.py:299-306), and the combat-ending and CanReceivePowers cases both imply the combat is over. Live the moment a power-amount modifier that can zero a self-buff is ported.
